sentences.text: Slot allocation within the Regional Flow Platform is governed by operational safety, published capacity, equitable access, and traceable collaborative decision making.
The Slot Allocation Engine is introduced in operating documentation with the local alias Blueharbor for controller-facing references during transition training.
The Slot Allocation Engine proposes regulated departure and arrival opportunities by matching demand from the Demand Prediction Service to constraints supplied by the Capacity Assessment Module.
The primary inputs are the Flight Intent Message, the Airport Capacity Plan, the current Airport Acceptance Rate, runway metering limits, and airspace sector loading conditions.
When a Ground Delay Program is active, the engine derives a Calculated Takeoff Time or arrival opportunity that preserves the declared capacity envelope before local preference is applied.
The Regional Flow Manager owns the final operating policy for priority classes and may authorize temporary rule changes during a Capacity Reduction State.
The Slot Coordinator administers the allocation run, reviews exceptions, and confirms that proposed results are ready for publication through the Airport CDM Portal.
Baseline priority is assigned first to safety-critical, emergency, humanitarian, and national obligation flights, subject to validation by the appropriate operational authority.
Scheduled commercial services are then handled according to the published timetable, declared readiness, airport acceptance capacity, and the fairness rules held in the Business Rules Registry.
General aviation, repositioning, training, and discretionary movements are allocated after protected and scheduled demand unless a specific operational justification is approved.
Fairness is measured across operators by delay distribution, proportional access to constrained capacity, and avoidance of systematic disadvantage over the active regulation period.
The engine shall not improve one operator's position by imposing an excessive delay on another operator unless the rule basis is visible and logged.
The Airline Interface Adapter supplies operator preferences, but those preferences are advisory unless they are consistent with the governing priority class and available capacity.
The Target Off Block Time is used to test readiness, and an aircraft that cannot meet readiness criteria may be resequenced behind aircraft that can use the opportunity.
The Airline Operations Coordinator uses the delay slip when requesting an exemption review for a crew connectivity constraint that is not already represented in the allocation data.
Exemption requests are evaluated against safety impact, network impact, passenger impact, crew legality, and the availability of a lower-impact alternative.
The Slot Coordinator records each accepted or rejected exemption in the Collaborative Decision Log with the rule applied, the approving role, and the expected operational consequence.
The Data Governance Steward ensures that exemption categories, priority codes, and fairness metrics are versioned in the Business Rules Registry before they are used in live allocation.
The Arrival Regulation Console presents proposed arrival opportunities with the capacity source, regulation start time, and expected delay for each affected flight.
The Departure Metering Service presents proposed departure opportunities and associated Calculated Takeoff Time values for coordination with the Tower Sequence Manager.
The Tower Supervisor may reject a proposed departure opportunity when runway safety, wake spacing, or local sequencing conditions make the proposal impracticable.
The Ramp Control Lead may identify apron constraints through the Ramp Movement Board, but the Slot Allocation Engine remains responsible for recalculating the regulated opportunity.
All allocation runs are time stamped by the Time Synchronization Service and written to the Audit Event Ledger for later reconstruction of the decision sequence.

During Normal Operations, allocation results are refreshed at regular intervals, while Adverse Weather Mode and Recovery Phase allow shorter recalculation cycles approved by the Regional Flow Manager.

If the Regional Flow Platform enters Contingency Fallback State, the Contingency Operations Console preserves the last valid allocation, supports manual amendments, and marks the resulting Slot Compliance State as provisional.

Post-event assessment in the Performance Analytics Warehouse compares proposed opportunities, actual movement times, exemption usage, and operator-level delay equity to improve subsequent rule calibration.
